content:
The image shows an opened soybean pod with two seeds (yellow-green and green) still attached. Key visual features:

- **White cottony/fluffy mycelial growth** visible at the base of the seeds inside the pod wall
- **Brown streaking and discoloration** of the inner pod wall
- Seeds still largely intact in shape but the pod interior is compromised
- The white fluffy material is concentrated at seed attachment points

The white cottony mycelium inside the pod is the hallmark sign of **White Mold** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). This pathogen produces abundant white fluffy mycelium inside pods and can colonize seeds within. The brown discoloration of the pod wall is consistent with tissue necrosis from this pathogen.

Phomopsis seed decay could cause chalky/shriveled seeds, but the seeds here look normal in shape. Fusarium doesn't typically produce this type of white cottony internal growth. The white mycelium inside the pod is the distinguishing feature.
